v3_architecture_constraints_derived_from.description: Observations that any V3 architecture proposal must reconcile. These are NOT decisions — they're constraints the decisions must satisfy.
constraints: C1: CSS variable definitions exist in SIX files with FOUR different roles (chrome-canonical, chrome-consumer-only, chrome-disguised-as-design, canvas-operational, canvas-operational-legacy-duplicate, dark-override-violation). Any two-bucket architecture is insufficient.
C2: Demo app depends on a file V2 treated as 'legacy dead' (components/Canvas/Canvas.css). Deleting without demo migration breaks the public editor-embed flow.
C3: ux-fixes.css is a chrome consumer that V2 completely missed. Every spec must enumerate themes/ directory contents before proposing renames.

C4: design-tokens.css defines GLOBAL :root --aqb-* tokens (layout/btn/input/icon) — it's a second chrome source competing with default.css. V3 must decide: merge into default.css, keep as separate chrome module, or reclassify these as a new 'output-tokens' namespace (these are tokens users' sites inherit).

C5: Canvas-operational tokens in editor/canvas/Canvas.css and components/Canvas/Canvas.css overlap heavily. V3 must decide if these are one thing or two, and whether one is truly legacy (audit diff needed).

C6: 'aqb' prefix is multi-semantic (CSS vars + keyframes + classnames + data attrs + storage keys + public API + user-export HTML). Renaming 'aqb' wholesale is NOT token-scope work. V3 must scope-scope each category.

C7: data-aqb-* and user-export class names (.aqb-hero-section etc.) appear in USER-EXPORTED HTML for Buildrik customers. Changing these is a breaking change for exported sites, not an internal rename.
C8: Storage keys migration has a precedent (storageMigration.ts mapping aquibra-* → aqb-*). Any storage key rename must follow that pattern.
C9: applyTheme() has ONE real caller (demo/main.tsx:21) contrary to V2 claim of zero. Deleting requires demo handling.
C10: Five undefined-but-consumed chrome tokens need decisions: either add definitions (pick values) or rename each consumer to a defined token. This is independent of any broader rename.
C11: Two orphan @keyframes references detected (aqb-slide-down in QuickSwitcher, aqb-bar-slide-up in AIAssistantBar) — these may be pre-existing bugs, not V3 scope, but flagged.

C12: Persisted design-token system at features/design-system writes --aqb-* strings to :root at runtime, but those strings don't exist in any CSS file's definitions — it's running on undefined-variable behavior today. V3 must acknowledge this as a PRE-EXISTING bug, not introduce it.

questions_for_v3_brainstorm_before_archi.description: Answer these before proposing any architecture. Answers inform whether a rename/namespace split is even the right tool.
questions: Q1: Is Buildrik the final product name? All 'aqb' → new-prefix migration presumes yes. Any historical name change incoming?
Q2: Is the editor's embedded-in-dashboard use the primary customer-facing surface, or is demo/main.tsx important too? Answer shapes whether breaking demo is acceptable.
Q3: Do Buildrik's customers (who use the editor) have exported HTML files in production? If yes, data-aqb-* and .aqb-* class renames are breaking changes that need separate compatibility planning.
Q4: Is the design-token user feature (Design tab in sidebar) shipped and used, or half-built? Codex flagged this as critical; V2 didn't confirm.
Q5: Is themes/ux-fixes.css intentional or a leftover file that should be merged into default.css?
Q6: Are the two Canvas.css files (editor/canvas/ and components/Canvas/) intentional duplicates for backwards compat, or should one be deleted?
Q7: Should design-tokens.css :root definitions merge into default.css, or stay separate as an 'output tokens' module?
Q8: Should canvas-operational tokens be renamed to a distinct namespace (e.g., --buildrick-canvas-op-*) or kept under chrome since they're not user-editable?

Q9: What's the rename strategy for data-aqb-* engine attributes that appear in exported HTML? (Option A: full rename with export migration, Option B: keep aqb- for export stability, rename only internals, Option C: version the attributes.)
Q10: Are the 500+ aqb-* CSS class names part of the 'aqb identity' that needs renaming, or are they product-namespaced and out of scope? Classes appearing in user exports especially need scrutiny.
